title: Founding of Epidamnos (Durrës)
description: Greek colonists from Corinth and Corcyra founded the coastal city of Epidamnos, later Dyrrhachium and modern Durrës, a key Adriatic port.

title: Roman Conquest of Illyria
description: Rome defeated the Illyrian kingdom under King Gentius, bringing the region of modern Albania under Roman control.

title: Skanderbeg's Rebellion Against the Ottomans
description: Gjergj Kastrioti, known as Skanderbeg, led a prolonged Albanian resistance against the Ottoman Empire from his stronghold at Krujë.

title: Albanian Declaration of Independence
description: Ismail Qemali proclaimed Albania's independence from the Ottoman Empire in Vlorë, establishing the modern Albanian state.

title: Communist Takeover Under Enver Hoxha
description: Enver Hoxha's partisans seized power, beginning over four decades of isolationist communist rule in Albania.

title: End of Communist Rule
description: Albania transitioned to a multiparty democracy as the communist system collapsed, ending decades of isolation.

title: Albania Joins NATO
description: Albania became a full member of the NATO alliance, marking its integration into Western security structures.

title: Foundation of the Co-Principality
description: The first paréage established Andorra as a co-principality ruled jointly by the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix, a system that endures today.

title: Creation of the Consell de la Terra
description: Andorra established the Council of the Land, one of Europe's oldest parliamentary bodies, to represent its parishes.

title: French Head of State Confirmed
description: A French edict confirmed the French head of state as co-prince of Andorra alongside the Bishop of Urgell.

title: Universal Male Suffrage Introduced
description: Following political unrest, Andorra extended voting rights to all adult men, modernizing its electoral system.

title: Women Gain the Right to Vote
description: Andorra granted women the right to vote, expanding democratic participation in the principality.

title: New Constitution and UN Membership
description: Andorra adopted its first written constitution as a parliamentary democracy and joined the United Nations.

title: Roman Province of Noricum Established
description: The Celtic kingdom of Noricum, covering much of modern Austria, was incorporated peacefully into the Roman Empire.

title: Habsburg Rule Begins
description: Rudolf I of Habsburg defeated Ottokar II at the Battle on the Marchfeld, beginning over six centuries of Habsburg rule in Austria.

title: First Ottoman Siege of Vienna
description: Vienna withstood a major siege by the Ottoman Empire under Suleiman the Magnificent, halting Ottoman expansion into Central Europe.

title: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
description: The Ausgleich created the dual monarchy of Austria-Hungary, granting Hungary autonomy under a shared Habsburg crown.

title: Founding of the Republic of Austria
description: After the collapse of Austria-Hungary in World War I, the First Austrian Republic was proclaimed in Vienna.

title: Anschluss with Nazi Germany
description: Nazi Germany annexed Austria in the Anschluss, ending Austrian independence until after World War II.

title: Austrian State Treaty and Neutrality
description: Austria regained full sovereignty as Allied occupation ended, and it declared permanent neutrality.

title: Austria Joins the European Union
description: Austria became a member of the European Union, deepening its integration into European economic and political structures.

title: First Mention of Minsk
description: Minsk, the future Belarusian capital, was first recorded in chronicles in connection with the Battle on the Nemiga River.

title: Union with Poland-Lithuania
description: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania, encompassing Belarusian lands, entered a dynastic union with Poland that shaped the region for centuries.

title: Francysk Skaryna Prints First Belarusian Book
description: Francysk Skaryna printed a Bible in a Slavic vernacular in Prague, pioneering printing in Eastern Europe.

title: Belarusian Lands Annexed by Russia
description: Following the partitions of Poland-Lithuania, Belarusian territories were incorporated into the Russian Empire.

title: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic Formed
description: The Byelorussian SSR was established, later becoming a founding republic of the Soviet Union.

title: Chernobyl Fallout Devastates Belarus
description: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster in neighboring Ukraine contaminated large areas of Belarus, causing lasting health and environmental harm.

title: Belarus Declares Independence
description: Belarus declared independence amid the dissolution of the Soviet Union, becoming a sovereign state.

title: Alexander Lukashenko Elected President
description: Alexander Lukashenko won Belarus's first presidential election and went on to dominate the country's politics for decades.

title: Caesar Conquers the Belgae
description: Julius Caesar subdued the Belgae tribes during the Gallic Wars, describing them as among the fiercest peoples of Gaul.

title: Battle of the Golden Spurs
description: Flemish militias defeated French knights at Kortrijk, a landmark victory celebrated in Flemish history.

title: Van Eyck Completes the Ghent Altarpiece
description: Jan van Eyck completed the Ghent Altarpiece, a masterpiece of Early Netherlandish painting in Flanders.

title: Belgian Revolution and Independence
description: Belgium broke away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, establishing an independent constitutional monarchy.

title: German Invasion in World War I
description: Germany invaded neutral Belgium, triggering British entry into World War I and devastating the country.

title: Treaty of Rome Hosts and Brussels EEC
description: Belgium became a founding member of the European Economic Community, with Brussels emerging as Europe's institutional center.

title: Belgium Becomes a Federal State
description: Constitutional reforms transformed Belgium into a federal state with autonomous Flemish, Walloon, and Brussels regions.

title: Roman Conquest of the Illyrians
description: Rome suppressed the Great Illyrian Revolt and consolidated control over the region of modern Bosnia within the province of Dalmatia.

title: Kingdom of Bosnia Founded
description: Tvrtko I was crowned king, establishing the medieval Kingdom of Bosnia as a powerful Balkan state.

title: Ottoman Conquest of Bosnia
description: The Ottoman Empire conquered the Kingdom of Bosnia, beginning over four centuries of Ottoman rule and Islamization.

title: Austro-Hungarian Administration Begins
description: The Congress of Berlin placed Bosnia and Herzegovina under Austro-Hungarian administration, ending Ottoman control.

title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
description: Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, triggering the outbreak of World War I.

title: Independence and Outbreak of War
description: Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence from Yugoslavia, soon followed by a devastating three-year war.

title: Dayton Peace Agreement
description: The Dayton Accords ended the Bosnian War, establishing the country's current decentralized political structure.

title: Founding of the First Bulgarian Empire
description: Khan Asparuh established the First Bulgarian Empire south of the Danube, recognized by Byzantium as a sovereign state.

title: Christianization Under Boris I
description: Boris I adopted Christianity as the state religion, integrating Bulgaria into the Christian European world.

title: Cyrillic Script Developed in Bulgaria
description: Disciples of Saints Cyril and Methodius developed the Cyrillic alphabet in Bulgaria, shaping Slavic literacy.

title: Ottoman Conquest of Bulgaria
description: The Ottoman Empire completed its conquest of Bulgaria, beginning nearly five centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: Liberation and Autonomous Principality
description: The Russo-Turkish War and the Treaty of Berlin created an autonomous Bulgarian principality, ending Ottoman domination.

title: Bulgaria Declares Full Independence
description: Bulgaria proclaimed full independence from the Ottoman Empire, elevating its ruler to the title of tsar.

title: Fall of the Communist Regime
description: The long-ruling communist leader Todor Zhivkov was ousted, beginning Bulgaria's transition to democracy.

title: Bulgaria Joins the European Union
description: Bulgaria became a member of the European Union, completing its post-communist integration with Europe.

title: Tomislav Crowned First King of Croatia
description: Tomislav is traditionally regarded as the first king of Croatia, uniting Croatian lands into a medieval kingdom.

title: Personal Union with Hungary
description: Croatia entered a personal union with the Kingdom of Hungary, shaping its political path for centuries.

title: Habsburg Rule Begins
description: Croatian nobles elected Ferdinand of Habsburg as king, bringing Croatia under Habsburg rule as a defense against the Ottomans.

title: Joining the Kingdom of Yugoslavia
description: After Austria-Hungary's collapse, Croatia joined the new Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia.

title: Croatia Declares Independence
description: Croatia declared independence from Yugoslavia, triggering the Croatian War of Independence.

title: End of the War of Independence
description: Operation Storm and subsequent agreements brought the Croatian War of Independence to an end, restoring state control.

title: Croatia Joins the European Union
description: Croatia became the 28th member of the European Union, marking its integration into the European community.

title: Cyril and Methodius in Great Moravia
description: The missionaries Cyril and Methodius arrived in Great Moravia, spreading Christianity and Slavonic liturgy among the Czechs.

title: Charles University Founded in Prague
description: Emperor Charles IV founded Charles University in Prague, the oldest university in Central Europe.

title: Jan Hus Burned at the Stake
description: Reformer Jan Hus was executed for heresy, sparking the Hussite movement and wars that shaped Czech identity.

title: Battle of White Mountain
description: Habsburg forces defeated the Bohemian estates, ushering in centuries of Habsburg dominance over the Czech lands.

title: Founding of Czechoslovakia
description: Czechoslovakia was established as an independent republic following the dissolution of Austria-Hungary.

title: Prague Spring and Soviet Invasion
description: Reforms during the Prague Spring were crushed when Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia.

title: Velvet Revolution
description: Peaceful protests during the Velvet Revolution ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia.

title: Establishment of the Czech Republic
description: Czechoslovakia peacefully split in the Velvet Divorce, creating the independent Czech Republic and Slovakia.

title: Harald Bluetooth Christianizes Denmark
description: King Harald Bluetooth converted the Danes to Christianity, commemorated on the Jelling runestones.

title: Cnut the Great Builds a North Sea Empire
description: The Danish king Cnut the Great ruled an empire spanning Denmark, England, and Norway.

title: Kalmar Union Formed
description: Queen Margaret I united Denmark, Norway, and Sweden under a single crown in the Kalmar Union.

title: Protestant Reformation in Denmark
description: Denmark officially adopted Lutheranism, establishing a state Protestant church under royal authority.

title: Denmark Adopts a Constitution
description: Denmark transitioned from absolute monarchy to constitutional monarchy with its first democratic constitution.

title: Abolition of Absolute Monarchy
description: The June Constitution ended centuries of absolutist royal rule and introduced parliamentary governance.

title: Denmark Joins the European Community
description: Denmark joined the European Economic Community, the first Nordic country to do so.

title: Danish Conquest of Tallinn
description: Danish forces under Valdemar II conquered northern Estonia, founding the city later known as Tallinn.

title: University of Tartu Founded
description: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden founded the University of Tartu, a lasting center of learning in Estonia.

title: Estonia Declares Independence
description: Estonia proclaimed independence amid the collapse of the Russian Empire, founding its first republic.

title: Soviet Annexation of Estonia
description: The Soviet Union occupied and annexed Estonia under the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, ending its independence.

title: The Baltic Way
description: Estonians joined a human chain across the Baltic states protesting Soviet rule and demanding independence.

title: Restoration of Independence
description: Estonia restored its independence as the Soviet Union collapsed, regaining full sovereignty.

title: Estonia Joins the EU and NATO
description: Estonia joined both the European Union and NATO, anchoring itself firmly in Western institutions.

title: Swedish Influence and Christianization
description: According to tradition, a Swedish crusade brought Christianity and Swedish rule to Finland in the mid-12th century.

title: Agricola Publishes Finnish New Testament
description: Mikael Agricola translated the New Testament into Finnish, laying the foundation for written Finnish.

title: Finland Becomes a Russian Grand Duchy
description: Sweden ceded Finland to Russia, which became an autonomous Grand Duchy under the tsar.

title: Universal Suffrage Introduced
description: Finland became the first country in Europe to grant women full voting and candidacy rights.

title: Finland Declares Independence
description: Finland declared independence from Russia amid the chaos of the Russian Revolution.

title: The Winter War
description: Finland resisted a Soviet invasion in the Winter War, preserving its independence despite territorial losses.

title: Finland Joins the European Union
description: Finland became a member of the European Union, deepening its ties with Western Europe.

title: Caesar Defeats Vercingetorix at Alesia
description: Julius Caesar's victory over the Gallic chieftain Vercingetorix completed the Roman conquest of Gaul.

title: Baptism of Clovis
description: The Frankish king Clovis converted to Catholic Christianity, uniting the Franks and founding a Christian kingdom.

title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
description: Charlemagne was crowned Emperor by the Pope in Rome, reviving imperial authority in Western Europe.

title: Execution of Joan of Arc
description: Joan of Arc, a key figure in the Hundred Years' War, was burned at the stake; she became a French national heroine.

title: The French Revolution Begins
description: The storming of the Bastille launched the French Revolution, overturning the monarchy and proclaiming liberty and equality.

title: Napoleon Crowned Emperor
description: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French, reshaping Europe through war and reform.

title: Eiffel Tower Completed
description: The Eiffel Tower was completed for the Paris World's Fair, becoming an enduring symbol of France.

title: Fifth Republic Established
description: Charles de Gaulle founded the Fifth Republic, creating France's current constitutional system.

title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
description: Germanic tribes under Arminius destroyed three Roman legions, halting Roman expansion east of the Rhine.

title: Otto I Founds the Holy Roman Empire
description: Otto I was crowned emperor, establishing the Holy Roman Empire that dominated German lands for centuries.

title: Gutenberg's Printing Press
description: Johannes Gutenberg developed movable-type printing in Mainz, revolutionizing the spread of knowledge.

title: Luther's Ninety-Five Theses
description: Martin Luther challenged Church practices, launching the Protestant Reformation from Wittenberg.

title: Unification of Germany
description: The German states united into the German Empire under Prussian leadership and Chancellor Otto von Bismarck.

title: Nazi Seizure of Power
description: Adolf Hitler became chancellor, leading to dictatorship, the Holocaust, and World War II.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: The Berlin Wall fell, symbolizing the end of the Cold War division of Germany.

title: German Reunification
description: East and West Germany reunified into a single democratic state after decades of division.

title: First Olympic Games
description: The first recorded Olympic Games were held at Olympia, a defining tradition of ancient Greek culture.

title: Birth of Athenian Democracy
description: The reforms of Cleisthenes established democracy in Athens, a foundational model for later governments.

title: Battles of Thermopylae and Salamis
description: Greek city-states resisted the Persian invasion, with decisive resistance at Thermopylae and victory at Salamis.

title: Reign of Alexander the Great Begins
description: Alexander the Great ascended the Macedonian throne and built an empire spreading Greek culture across Asia.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: The Ottoman conquest of Constantinople ended the Byzantine Empire, bringing Greek lands under Ottoman rule.

title: Greek War of Independence Begins
description: Greeks rose against Ottoman rule, launching the war that led to an independent Greek state.

title: First Modern Olympic Games in Athens
description: Athens hosted the first modern Olympic Games, reviving the ancient tradition.

title: Greece Joins the European Community
description: Greece became a member of the European Economic Community, integrating with Western Europe.
